- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% if recent price is falling.
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by forecast overshoot, apply “lag correction”: reduce forecast by 5–10% in next 2–3 periods.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion after a strong move (e.g., 70→60), model often fails to revert; forecast should be adjusted toward historical mean of last 5–7 days.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overreact to sentiment shifts; apply “sentiment dampening”: reduce forecast magnitude by 0.5–1.5x sentiment magnitude if sentiment >0.7.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “0.00” or “-0.50”, model often underperforms; increase forecast by 2–4% to compensate for low sentiment bias.
